name: Intellia Therapeutics, Inc. (Nasdaq: NTLA)
upcoming_dates: 2026-11-05 | earnings | Q3 2026 earnings release and call, estimated before market open | https://www.marketbeat.com/stocks/NASDAQ/NTLA/earnings/ | aggregator
2027-03-10 | PDUFA | FDA PDUFA target action date for the lonvo-z BLA in hereditary angioedema | https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1652130/000119312526385194/ntla-ex99_1.htm | primary
product: Lonvo-z, formerly NTLA-2002, a one-time in vivo CRISPR therapy that inactivates KLKB1 to lower kallikrein for HAE. Nex-z, formerly NTLA-2001, for ATTR-CM and ATTRv-PN with Regeneron. REGV131-LNP1265 in hemophilia B is led by Regeneron; AVC-201 and AVC-203 come from AvenCell using licensed Intellia technology.
demand: HAE affects about one in 50,000 people and causes severe, unpredictable, potentially life-threatening attacks; 71% of HAELO patients entered on long-term prophylaxis, and 20% reported complete control on prior therapy. ATTR is large, growing and highly underdiagnosed, with patients still progressing on approved stabilizers and silencers.
pricing_power: Not found. Intellia is pre-revenue and disclosed no price for lonvo-z. Management argues a one-time therapy can be positioned against lifelong prophylaxis, but no payer, reimbursement or pricing data was disclosed in the sources read.
competition: HAE: Takeda Takhzyro, BioCryst Orladeyo, CSL Behring, and oral agents from Pharvaris and KalVista. ATTR: Alnylam Amvuttra, Pfizer tafamidis, BridgeBio acoramidis, Ionis and AstraZeneca eplontersen. Gene editing peers include CRISPR Therapeutics, Editas, Beam and Verve. Lonvo-z claims first one-time in vivo CRISPR positioning.
team: Led by CEO John Leonard, M.D., and CFO Edward Dulac; Jason Fredette is VP of Investor Relations and Corporate Communications. The 2026 annual meeting on 2026-06-10 approved all proposals, including director elections, auditor ratification and executive compensation, with no stockholder questions raised.
market_strategy: Launch lonvo-z in the US in H1 2027 through HAE treatment centers, using completed field medical, reimbursement and strategic accounts teams plus the HAEreframed.com disease awareness campaign. Fund partly with non-dilutive OrbiMed debt. Advance nex-z in ATTR with Regeneron and progress early pipeline programs including hemophilia B and AvenCell assets.
bull: FDA accepted lonvo-z BLA with Priority Review and 2027-03-10 PDUFA, no advisory committee; $400M non-dilutive OrbiMed loan; cash $628.4M into 2028; Evercore upgraded to Outperform 2026-08-07.
bear: Q2 2026 revenue $7.66M missed $12.98M consensus, down 46%; $106.6M net loss; nex-z Grade 4 liver transaminase elevations tied to HLA C0501; Goldman Sell $9, Wolfe Underperform; consensus Hold.
falsifier: FDA issues a complete response letter for the lonvo-z BLA on or before the 2027-03-10 PDUFA date, or the label requires HLA/liver monitoring.
web_what_changed: 2026-09-08 FDA accepted the lonvo-z BLA for HAE with Priority Review and a PDUFA date of 2027-03-10, no advisory committee planned. 2026-09-04 Intellia signed a $400M non-dilutive OrbiMed senior secured term loan, $75M funded upfront and $325M milestone-gated. 2026-08-06 Q2 results: cash $628.4M into 2028, nex-z Phase 3 enrollment resumed, HLA C0501 safety finding. 2026-06-13 HAELO data at EAACI and NEJM.
web_not_known_yesterday: Not found. No new primary company disclosure dated 2026-09-24 or 2026-09-25 was found; the newest material primary filing remains the 2026-09-08 BLA acceptance and PDUFA date. The investor relations Upcoming Events section reads More events are coming soon, and the stock closed 2026-09-24 at $12.16.
web_demand_price_volume_mix: Not yet applicable. Intellia is pre-revenue, so growth is not coming from product demand, price, volume or mix. Q2 2026 collaboration revenue was $7.66M versus $14.2M a year earlier, down about 46% and below the $12.98M consensus, driven by lower Regeneron revenue. Product volume begins only with a possible H1 2027 launch.
web_suppliers: Not found by name. Intellia relies on third-party contract manufacturers, collaborators and licensors, which its own filings list as risk factors; no specific CDMO or lipid-nanoparticle supplier is disclosed. Regeneron is the ATTR development and commercialization partner, sharing 25% of worldwide costs and profits with a US co-promotion option.
web_customers: Effectively one: Regeneron, the source of essentially all collaboration revenue, $7.66M in Q2 2026, with 25% ATTR cost and profit sharing and a US co-promotion option. Future end customers are HAE patients, roughly one in 50,000 people, and, through Regeneron, ATTR patients. Concentration is extreme and revenue is falling.
web_who_loses: Chronic HAE prophylaxis makers: Takeda with Takhzyro, BioCryst with Orladeyo, CSL Behring, plus oral competitors Pharvaris and KalVista. In ATTR: Alnylam with Amvuttra and patisiran, Pfizer with tafamidis, BridgeBio with acoramidis, Ionis and AstraZeneca with eplontersen. Also CRISPR peers CRISPR Therapeutics, Editas, Beam and Verve.
web_contradicting_evidence: nex-z caused Grade 4 liver transaminase elevations in under 1% of MAGNITUDE patients, associated with HLA C0501, and prior clinical holds halted dosing. Q2 2026 revenue missed consensus, $7.66M versus $12.98M, with a $106.6M net loss. Consensus rating is Hold, not Buy; Goldman Sachs rates Sell at $9 and Wolfe downgraded to Underperform. Eplontersen CARDIO-TTRansform missed.
web_if_management_right: Lonvo-z wins FDA approval by the 2027-03-10 PDUFA as the first in vivo CRISPR therapy and only one-time HAE treatment, launching in the US in H1 2027 while cash funds operations into 2028. nex-z becomes a one-time ATTR therapy, and its event-driven MAGNITUDE trial shows benefit on top of tafamidis in a large underdiagnosed market.
web_if_management_wrong: FDA issues a complete response letter or restricts the lonvo-z label, for example requiring HLA or liver monitoring. nex-z transaminase safety caps the ATTR program, forcing redesign or another hold. With $628.4M cash but a $400M milestone-gated debt facility, a delay drives further dilution and restrictive covenants.
web_second_order_beneficiaries: Regeneron, taking 25% of ATTR economics plus hemophilia B milestones. OrbiMed as lender. Contract manufacturers and lipid-nanoparticle suppliers. HLA genotyping and diagnostics labs. CRISPR peers Editas, CRISPR Therapeutics, Beam and Caribou if in vivo editing is validated. AvenCell, which licenses Intellia allogeneic cell engineering technology.
